Ellis, L.D., Badel, A.F., Chiang, M.L., Park, R.J.-Y. and Chiang, Y.-M. (2020). Toward electrochemical synthesis of cement - An electrolyzer-based process for decarbonating CaCO3 while producing useful gas streams. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 117(23), 12584-12591. doi:10.1073/pnas.1821673116 (first published 16 September 2019; Sackler Colloquium paper).

Locators are printed page numbers (12584-12591; PDF has 8 pages). A laboratory proof-of-concept paper; the only technology-level numbers are in the Discussion energy analysis (SI Appendix not held): 5.2-7.1 MJ electrical per kg cement, with the assumed efficiencies. No capex or opex is given (authors say a techno-economic analysis is out of scope). The 5.2-7.1 MJ/kg figure is an end-to-end electricity input for the H2-fired-kiln configuration; it already includes making the kiln heat from H2, so it is not additive to kiln fuel. The paper's cost comparisons (USD 28-100/t cement energy, USD 91 vs <40/t CO2 capture) are in other-values with no price year. Two-column PDF: pdftotext -layout interleaves columns; non-layout mode was used.
